A1.justification: Despite renaming GENIE to EKS and changing the title, both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-conditioned NeRF editing work. All 14 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on NeRF-Synthetic and Mip-NeRF 360, component ablations, rendering-speed measurements and editing simulations.

after.justification: v2 reports original static and edited-scene reconstruction results, component ablations and physics-based editing comparisons in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v2 changes RT-GPS from spherical candidates ordered by mean distance to ellipsoidal candidates ordered by Mahalanobis distance, using full covariance. It replaces opacity-based densification with gradient-based cloning/splitting and introduces Kabsch-based view-direction restoration and tetrahedral editing instead of triangle soup. These substantially revise training and editing procedures.

E1.justification: NeRF-Synthetic, Mip-NeRF 360, Fox and custom assets remain represented. v2 adds wind-driven Ficus and particle-impact Fox scenarios in Figure 9. The Chen et al. editing benchmark already appeared qualitatively in v1, so its new numerical evaluation does not constitute a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The static NeRF-Synthetic comparison adds INGP, GaMeS, Point-NeRF and NeuralEditor, while removing NeRF, Nerfacto, VolSDF, ENVIDR, Plenoxels and GS; LagHash and RIP-NeRF remain. In qualitative editing, GaMeS replaces Point-NeRF between v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 8. v2 also evaluates PhysGaussian and GASP in physics comparisons, rather than merely citing them.

E3.justification: v2 adds ground-truth-based PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS evaluation for the previously qualitative editing benchmark. Its ablation design separately evaluates static and edited reconstructions, while v1's FPS evaluation disappears. These substantially change the evaluation design; omission of v1's training settings does not establish that training budgets changed.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix B tests neighbor counts, Gaussian radii, encoding, densification, pruning, learnable means and appearance embeddings. v2 replaces this with targeted Euclidean-KNN, hash-grid-distillation and view-direction-restoration ablations across static and edited scenes, plus qualitative evidence in Figures 5 and 10. v1's explicit mesh-discontinuity and insufficient-Gaussian failure cases are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Gaussian confidence parameters concern the method, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Static reconstruction values change, such as Lego PSNR from 33.84 to 35.59 in Table 1, but matching training settings are not established. v2 adds edited-scene scores, revised ablations and physics comparisons. EKS leads all eight editing PSNR columns, but not every other metric: Drums SSIM is 0.910 versus GaMeS's 0.914. v1's Mip-NeRF 360 numerical results and FPS table are removed.

T1.justification: The main-text interpolation specification relaxes the covariance restriction from diagonal to full anisotropic covariance. However, the RT-GPS bounded-error derivation is retained essentially unchanged from v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix B. The newly emphasized affine-equivariance claim receives no separate theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a GS/NeRF hybrid with fast proximity search and unusually broad physics integration to an affine-equivariant kernel encoding that preserves feature structure under transformations. v2 foregrounds training-time hash-grid distillation and grid-free inference, while dropping earlier novelty assertions about the extent of physics integration and editable unbounded scenes.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting neighborhood stability to Mahalanobis distance, appearance preservation to view-direction restoration, and sparse visual artifacts to small PSNR changes in the distillation ablation. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning sparse Gaussians, excessive stretching and mesh discontinuities, without demonstrating that those failure conditions have been resolved.

D1.justification: v1 specifies 20,000 training steps, an RTX 3090, neighbor counts, quantiles, initialization procedures and densification/pruning thresholds and schedules. v2 removes this implementation-settings section without equivalent appendix documentation. It adds transformation-handling details and changes the stated code location from genie to eks, but substantially reduces experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work against deformation-sensitive point encodings and fixed-grid representations. In particular, v1 describes similarity to LagHash, whereas v2 emphasizes its distinction through grid-free inference. The bibliography also adds NeRFiller and removes works including SuGaR, Mani-GS and GS-Deformer, accompanying the move away from positioning primarily around GS editing tools.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Splash Grid Encoding is reorganized into kernel encoding and feature-distillation explanations, with a separate view-direction-restoration subsection. Sections become numbered, ablations move into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized. This exceeds a terminology or formatting update.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening illustration, substantially redraws the pipeline and RT-GPS diagrams, and adds neighborhood, physics-comparison and ablation figures. Retained simulation panels are rearranged and relocated. Tables are restructured for edited-scene evaluation, while speed and real-scene tables disappear. Appendix Figures 11–12 enlarge the main qualitative comparison rather than add independent experiments.

improvement.justification: v2 better substantiates the paper's central editing claim: Tables 2–3 add quantitative editing comparisons and ablations that distinguish static reconstruction from behavior after deformation, supported by clearer diagrams and enlarged qualitative results. The net gain is limited by removal of implementation settings, runtime and real-scene numerical evidence, and explicit failure cases. These losses prevent a stronger overall improvement judgment.
